page: Microsoft Azure DC16ads_cc_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCADCCV5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 614 GB local disk with Premium Storage capability, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% of tested hardware, while multi-core performance remains in the average tier. Memory subsystem testing reveals a notable performance tradeoff: while Passmark memory scores are strong and read-only small-block memory bandwidth is average, the large-block write bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. In application-specific benchmarks, the server delivers average throughput for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation, alongside strong text generation speeds during small-scale LLM inference.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the DC16ads_cc_v5 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and local storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, 64 GB of RAM, and a 614 GB local disk makes this server type appropriate for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, static web serving, and intermediate-scale software development environments.
